title: O THAT Thou Wouldst the Heavens Rent
description: O THAT Thou Wouldst the Heavens Rent in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 9 verses and a piano.
about: John Wesley printed these words in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 138. They first appeared in a book he and his brother Charles published together, and the Collection's own index cannot say which of the two wrote them.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Common Metre (8.6.8.6), and this page sets them to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O THAT thou wouldst the hea-vens rent, In maj-es-ty come down; Stretch out thine arm om-ni-po-tent, And seize me for thine own!

lines: O THAT thou wouldst the heavens rent,
And seize me for thine own!
Descend, and let thy lightning burn
Thou only canst drive back the tide,
And bid the sun stand still.
What though I cannot break my chain,
Or e'er throw off my load?
Is there a thing too hard for thee,
Whose threatening looks dry up the sea,
Who, shall in thy presence stand,
Ungrasp the hold of thy right hand,
Sworn to destroy, let earth assail;
Stronger than all the powers of hell,
Lo! to the hills I lift mine eye,
Salvation in that name is found
A medicine for my every wound,
All, all I want is there!

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788; John Wesley died in 1791.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788) or John Wesley (1703–1791), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
